All 6 arrows executed with camera scrolls. Dumping the final board to look for the pad.Group (416-418) is L6 attempt 1's pad. Let me dump it with context.Critical finding: the ONLY state difference was red's position (E4 in attempt 2, absent in attempt 1). Checking whether the flower exists in earlier levels as a static feature.Checking L6's initial state to count total pegs and see the starting camera.Re-examining board 417's band structure east of the panel wall (world >113) carefully.**Strategic briefing — L6 attempt 2, 54/64 used, 1 green peg (S, in cart A) + red at E2.**

Major mechanics solved this turn by mining the L2 history: gray pegs = stuck pieces, and the purple flower is a **soft-reset button** (clicking its white center in L2 respawned all pegs), not a goal. Attempt-1's gray+flower simply meant "all pieces stuck." So reaching 1 peg doesn't clear L6 — the win must involve the never-seen far-east structure (world 124+, rows 40-59), reachable only via the narrow east corridor of cells (E5, E6, ...). Clicks are capped at the screen edge, so I must scroll the camera east by driving the peg-carrying cart past the dock junction before any leapfrogging.

**Turn 97 briefing.** The shaft hypothesis is dead — both Up presses were no-ops, so no hidden vessels exist; the level contains exactly two boxes. One asymmetry stands out: the right box perched at (C8,B7) ignored the westward slide, so vertical-top docks pin vessels — meaning the wire 53-54 "highway" is unproven. The left box can reach that wire via vertical 7-8 (which crosses it at rows 53-54), giving a clean test: if it slides east along the wire, I can ferry it under the grid to (C8,B8) and then test whether green#2 may jump down over the B7 box onto it — landing-on-box legality was never actually tested in L7.

[PLAN]
**Turn 98 briefing.** The highway is a mirage — "wire 53-54" is just the grid's bottom border (twin of the top border at row 16), so the box stays pinned at (C0,B7) and the two bottom-wire segments are permanently disconnected. That exhausts every vessel-routing idea: boxes can only ever occupy (C0,B4-B8), the notch, and the three right-segment docks — none of which produces a legal green jump. The level must therefore hinge on an untested interaction. Prime suspect: the grid seats share the exact sprite of L7's mobile container seats — if seats are clickable/movable, planting one at (C4,B2) unlocks a full seat-chain across the grid for green#1.

Two blues sit conveniently in the second row above the annex, and at least one more green waits at the panel's far-west top corner. Once the cart docks inside, the green can disembark northward over the blues and the capture campaign resumes.
